title: You can be the strong one in the room…
paragraphs:
You can be the strong one in the room…
and still go home exhausted.
That’s the part nobody talks about.

When you’re spiritually ahead, people lean on you.
They expect your wisdom.
Your patience.
Your prayers.
Your steadiness.

You become the one who understands first.
The one who forgives first.
The one who stays calm first.
The one who carries what others don’t even notice.
And yes—there is honor in that.
But there is also weight.

Because being spiritually mature does not mean you do not feel pain.
It means you often feel it deeply… and still choose obedience.

You see the compromise others call “normal.”
You notice the distance before others realize God feels far.
You fight battles in prayer that nobody else even knows exist.
Quiet battles.
Heavy ones.

Sometimes the hardest part is not resisting sin.
It is resisting resentment.

Resentment that you always have to be the one to understand.
The one to bend.
The one to take the high road.
The one to keep your heart soft when everyone else gets to stay careless.
But here’s what we miss:
Jesus knows exactly what it feels like to be spiritually ahead.

He was surrounded by people who misunderstood Him, doubted Him, used Him for miracles, and left Him in His darkest hour.
Yet He still loved.
Still served.
Still wept.
Still obeyed.
“He was despised and rejected by men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief…” — Isaiah 53:3
So if you feel tired because you’ve been carrying more spiritually than the people around you, hear this clearly:

Your burden is not proof that God has abandoned you.
It may be evidence that He has trusted you.
But He never asked you to carry it alone.

The danger of being spiritually ahead is pride.
The temptation is isolation.
The lie is, “Nobody pours into me, so I just have to survive.”
No.

Christ is still your Shepherd.
Christ is still your strength.
Christ is still the One who restores your soul.

Even leaders need washing.
Even disciplers need discipleship.
Even the strong need the Savior.

Come back to the feet of Jesus.
Not as the one with answers.
Not as the mature one.
Not as the strong one.
Just as His.

Because the cross was never only for the broken people around you.
It was for you too.

And the same grace you keep extending to others—
Jesus is extending to you right now.
Rest there.

Let Him hold the weight of being “ahead.”
Let Him protect your heart from bitterness.
Let Him remind you that maturity is not carrying everyone.
Maturity is staying close to Christ while you serve them.
You do not have to become hard to become holy.
You do not have to bleed in silence forever.
You do not have to be everybody’s rock when Jesus is yours.
